newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope calls for courage to stop violence.
newsitem.headline: Pope calls for courage to stop violence.

text.p: Pope John Paul urged world leaders on Sunday to act with timely courage to prevent senseless bloodshed.

He told pilgrims in St Peter's Square that divine mercy should "inspire in those who have the responsibility of government, at national and international levels, the necessary courage to intervene with timely wisdom in difficult situations before they reach breakdown and more blood is shed senselessly".
The Polish Pontiff did not refer to any country by name but has used his regular Sunday address in the past to call for calm in chaotic Albania and Zaire, which is hit by civil war.
An international security force, under Italian command, is preparing to deploy in Albania, where armed anarchy broke out last month in the wake of the collapse of shady investment schemes.
In Zaire, United Nations officials began organising an airlift of refugees but the advance of rebels seeking President Mobutu Sese Seko's resignation dimmed ceasefire prospects.
The Pope urged pilgrims not to think of violence as something inevitable or irrelevant because it happens far away.
